sdk.note: unitree_sdk2 ships a dedicated h2/ example folder (github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2/tree/main/example, accessed 2026-09-21) alongside g1, h1, r1, confirming H2 support in the same generic Unitree SDK; unitree_ros2 layers ROS2 on top via CycloneDDS.

order_type.note: Standard H2 is listed with a direct price on Unitree's own storefront; only the EDU customization variant requires contacting sales ('Please contact our sales team ... to purchase the EDU edition'). The standard listing was marked unavailable at time of access (stock/queue status), which does not change the storefront's cart-based order mechanism.

notes: The walking speed field notes the H2 is a deliberate step down from the H1's top speed in exchange for dexterity: 'the H1 was celebrated for its record-breaking speed of 3.3 m/s, the H2 is rated for under 2 m/s' (Humanoids Daily, 2025-10-20). We recorded the H1's superseded top speed as the H2 value here is only bounded ('under 2 m/s'); treat 7.2 km/h (2 m/s) as an upper bound, not a measured figure.

The task brief asked to pick H1 or H2 and name the other: H2 (announced 2025-10-20) is Unitree's direct successor to the H1 (announced 2019), replacing its 'R-A-F' hip layout with 'F-A-R' and adding a 3-DOF waist and up to three Jetson Orin NX modules. H1 itself remains for sale separately and is not covered by this file.

Unitree's own shop page does not state battery runtime or payload; both are omitted rather than sourced from secondary aggregators (RoboZaps, Humanoid.guide) that were not independently verified against a primary page during this build.
No named-customer delivery evidence was found; delivery.status stays 'claimed' (store listing only, no unboxing/serial/customs record located).

Capabilities research (2026-09-20): Unitree's own 'daily training video' releases show the H2 doing flying kicks, backflips, sandbag strikes and a boxing spar with a G1 (Interesting Engineering, 2025-12/2026-01 coverage), but none of these map cleanly onto this dataset's fixed capability ids (no 'acrobatics'/'combat' id exists, and a single flip or kick is not the sustained aerial-phase gait the 'run' id requires). None of the coverage states who or what controlled the robot during these clips -- Interesting Engineering instead describes teleoperation as a general 'transitional technology' for Unitree's humanoids without confirming it for this footage -- so per the schema's silence rule any such entry would have to be 'unknown' autonomy anyway. No hand DOF, tactile-skin, depth-camera or onboard-compute figure could be traced to a primary Unitree page (shop.unitree.com/products/unitree-h2 does not list them; unitree.com/h2 404s); secondary aggregator figures (e.g. Sharpa Wave 22-DOF hands cited by RoboZaps/Humanoid.guide) were not added for the same reason battery/payload were omitted above. capabilities left empty for this build.

locomotion left out (2026-09-21): searched the manufacturer's own product/press page and its main launch coverage (The Robot Report / IEEE Spectrum / named outlet where applicable) for a literal quote naming the propulsion ("bipedal", "legs", "walks", "wheeled base", etc.); none of the pages fetched in this pass contained a checkable sentence naming it specifically for H2 -- most pages describe height/DOF/speed without ever stating the locomotion type in words. Left out rather than inferred from photos or category. Revisit with a source that states it directly.
